test.title: Permutation and Combination - Test 6
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: Numbers are to be formed between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3000</mn></math>, which are divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>, using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> without repetition of digits. Then the total number of such numbers is _______.

Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> be distinct integers where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>25</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>25</mn></math>. Then, the number of ways of choosing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></math> is divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> , is _____ .

Let the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></math> be in A.P. Nine-digit numbers are to be formed using each of these three digits thrice such that three consecutive digits are in A.P. at least once. How many such numbers can be formed?

All the arrangements, with or without meaning, of the word <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>FARMER</mi></math> are written excluding any word that has two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> appearing together. The arrangements are listed serially in the alphabetic order as in the English dictionary. Then the serial number of the word <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>FARMER</mi></math> in this list is _____ .

The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>-digit natural numbers, such that the product of their digits is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn></math>, is

Number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>-digit numbers (the repetition of digits is allowed) which are made using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> , and are divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math> , is equal to

The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>-letter words, with or without meaning, each consisting of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> vowels and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> consonants, which can be formed from the letters of the word UNIVERSE without repetition is _____.
If the number of seven-digit numbers, such that the sum of their digits is even, is $m \cdot n \cdot 10^{\mathrm{n}}$; $m, n \in\{1,2,3, \ldots, 9\}$, then $m+n$ is equal to _______

The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>-digit numbers which are neither multiple of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn></math> nor multiple of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> is <u>           </u> .

The students <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>10</mn></msub></math> are to be divided into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> groups <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> such that each group has at least one student and the group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> has at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> students. Then the total number of possibilities of forming such groups is __________.

Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> be a non-negative integer. Then the number of divisors of the form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> of the number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mn>10</mn></mfenced><mn>10</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mfenced><mn>11</mn></mfenced><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mfenced><mn>13</mn></mfenced><mn>13</mn></msup></math> is equal to _____.

The number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn></math>-digit numbers which are multiples of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn></math> and are formed using all the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> is _____.

Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></math>. Then the number of elements in the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></math> and the sum of all the elements of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is not a multiple of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>}</mo></math> is

A boy needs to select five courses from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn></math> available courses, out of which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> courses are language courses. If he can choose at most two language courses, then the number of ways he can choose five courses is

The total number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>-digit numbers whose greatest common divisor with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> , is

The number of natural numbers lying between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1012</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>23421</mn></math> that can be formed using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></math> (repetition of digits is not allowed) and divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>55</mn></math> is _____.

The total number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>-digit numbers whose greatest common divisor with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> is _____.

Five digit numbers are formed using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>7</mn></math> with repetitions and are written in descending order with serial numbers. For example, the number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>77777</mn></math> has serial number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>. Then the serial number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>35337</mn></math> is

A number is called a palindrome if it reads the same backward as well as forward. For example <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>285582</mn></math> is a six digit palindrome. The number of six digit palindromes, which are divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>55</mn><mo>,</mo></math> is ________.

If all the six digit numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math> are arranged in the increasing order, then the sum of the digits in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>72</mn><mtext>th </mtext></msup></math> number is _______.
